confidence_notes: Beer, coffee, inexpensive meal and mid-range meal for two are anchored on Numbeo's Córdoba (Spain) figures as summarised in web search results (numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Cordoba-Spain, dated May 2026). Those figures were about €3.00 for a 0.5 L draught beer, €2.02 for a cappuccino, €12 for an inexpensive meal and about €50 for a mid-range meal for two. Figures vary between Numbeo pages. I cross-checked them against review-site reports of €10-15 set lunch menus. I shaded beer slightly lower because a local caña is smaller than 0.5 L. Searches found no reliable Córdoba (Spain) cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices, since results were mostly Córdoba, Argentina or single venues. Those two are therefore estimated from the local beer price (cocktail about 2.5x beer, wine glass about 1.05x beer) plus general Andalusian bar knowledge. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for a July low-season (extreme heat) window. No accommodation prices or live listings were checked. Euro prices were converted to USD at roughly the cross rate implied by RBA quotes. The FX observation was read from a web search summary of the RBA exchange-rates page, not from the page itself. Accommodation, cocktail and wine are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Core restaurant anchors use Córdoba-specific Numbeo figures. Cocktail, wine and lodging are scaled from general knowledge of mid-sized Andalusian heritage cities such as Seville and Granada. Córdoba is typically somewhat cheaper than those two, especially in July when extreme heat lowers hotel demand.
